A single drop of sweat made its way from my hairline, down between my eyes. Or maybe it was blood. Adrenaline heightened my senses in ways I thought impossible, making me see everything, feel everything. The restaurant was not even recognizable anymore. Everything was flipped, smashed or bloodied. And yet they kept on coming. My cover was being shredded from behind, I knew it was over. At this point I didn't care. In fact, my greatest annoyance was the sound of screaming between the gunshots. The bitch that I shot was crying like a bitch. I had two bullets left in my magazine. Perfect. The screaming ceased, and I jammed another magazine into my gun with great satisfaction.

These guys had no idea what they were sent into. Crying, pleading, without a fucking clue. I did not pity them for being put down. I pitied them for choosing the wrong side. A grenade flew across the room and into the wall. It was time to go. In a single move I got up and turned towards the point of origin. The flashbang partly blinded me, but I already had my aim. A guy hit the dirt, but I was not even remotely done. Strafing away from my cover I kept sending bullets across the room in the style of whack-a-mole. A bullet strafed my left side, but adrenaline told me I didn't care. Three down... Four...

Another grenade came at me. Not flying this time, but curling across the floor. In reflex I dodged to the side, but I knew there wouldn't be time...

Bullets - Archive

Sheets of rain fall as the cyborgs are closing in. I turn the corner and reach the market not long before a spherical droid scans the crowd.

The police droid spots me. I'm twenty feet away behind a fried octopus stand when a laser cuts by me, only to singe my shoulder. I quickly turn around and nuke it out of existence. I run into the first alley I reach and past a bookie, circling the stair ways. They wind up and up, and silhouettes below me are cast in red and blue.

I reach the roof with nowhere to go. I hop up on the ledge and look down, with my carbon fiber trench coat blowing with a gust.

"FREEZE! You are in violation of the Freedom of Movement Act, Section Two! You are not to move another muscle or we may open fire!"

I look down from the ledge for her. I spot her directly below, as she looks up at me. From her viewpoint, there is a glimmer, coming closer and closer, shining more and more before she snatches it four feet from the ground. It's a CPU diamond. "Got it!" she yells up to me.

"Lower your guns" a detective says, pushing through the crowd of police droids on the roof. "Disarm."

The droids comply as I turn around and fire lasers into the detectives chest. It heats up his chest cavity and burns a hole before the sergeant can eke out a, "No." and falls to his knees, then face plants to the ground.

I close my eyes and let the bullets push me over the edge, falling fast. Neon lights and colors whiz by. I land near her, and she throws my body on the back of her moto, while bullets whiz down from the roof tops.

They assume I'm dead, because I am dead. But, it's 2055, and I'll be alive again, before too long. It's just a matter of time before I am boosting again on these black streets.

I came up through the ranks of organized crime, an organization known for making all those opposed "disappear." We had many hitmen, but when an important hit was ordered I was the man for the job.

The hero is a badass detective tasked with taking down our whole operation. We enter into a cat-and-mouse game when there's a meeting of diplomats in the city, many of which are planning a trading reform that could put us out of business. I'm tasked with taking out our enemies. As set forth to remove the life from each diplomat systematically, I nearly escape each situation. The detective and his team are getting closer and closer. Tensions are high in the city, media is losing their minds, police and national guard are everywhere.

Despite the tight security, I find my way across the city to a top floor of a derelict office building with an open floor plan, watching and waiting for my target. He comes into view, cue the music. I line up my shot. At just before the 0:50 mark I hear a heavy footstep and the familiar sound of a pulled hammer behind me. The music stops and we stare each other down: it's the detective and he's serious. So am I.

Music starts again at the 0:50 second mark as I manage to defensively strike him and make some distance. Cue a volley of shots, dramatic cut scenes and debris flying for the next 3:00 or so. Near the end of that period, we get into a fist fight and I have him pinned at 3:56. I'm choking him out and he's losing the battle. Flashbacks of the hero's life and family, our previous encounters, the whole nine yards. At 4:40, you hear a gunshot and my body goes limp. The detective catches his breath and looks to the doorway to see that his previously absent partner caught up and delivered the shot that put this case to rest.

I had a the missing piece of information that the detective needed in my pocket, he would finally have what he needed to bring us all down. The diplomats are safe, though talks are understandably delayed for a while. Our hero passes on the relevant information to his partner and leaves.

He goes straight home, his wife meets him at the door. It's about this time he realizes that his wife is actually a monster from the paleolithic era.
